_readme: Every metric that can enter the Fundability score. Rule: each metric must tie to a LIHTC funding mechanism (QAP points, threshold, tiebreaker, award limit, basis boost); community need and opportunity belong to the Need and Opportunity tools. To add one: (1) add a column to fundability_site/data/tracts.geojson (build it in pipelines/fundability/build_fund_features.py), (2) add an entry below. Fields: id, column, label, group ('siteline' = scored, 'context' = shown but never scored), qap_section, qap_title, qap_ref, source, format (points|pct|count|number|years|flag|score), direction ('higher' or 'lower' is better for funding), scale ('points' uses max_points, 'percentile' ranks ARC tracts, 'flag' is 0/1), missing ('best'|'worst'|'skip'), in_fundability (default on/off), weight (default), description, measures (what the metric measures, one short paragraph), targets (which part of DCA's scoring it targets). Optional: 'breakdown' (sub-scores shown under the metric, never scored separately) and 'details' (supporting values shown under the metric).
weights_source: Fundability = SiteLine's location score (weight 100). The 2026-10-15 backtest and metric audit found that SiteLine, driven by transit (§XII) and schools (§XIII), is the only location measure that predicted which ARC applications DCA funded; the other layers added nothing on held-out rounds, so they are shown as context, not scored. See Methodology → Why these weights.

qap.title: State of Georgia 2024-2025 Qualified Allocation Plan

groups.title: Scored: SiteLine location score
groups.note: SiteLine's geographic QAP scoring, used exactly as provided. The tract value is its best 0.25-mile grid cell (median cell shown for comparison). This is the whole Fundability score.

groups.title: Context (shown, not scored)
groups.note: Funding rules that matter for whether a deal works or how ties break, but that didn't predict past awards. Shown for judgment; they don't change the score.

metrics.label: SiteLine location score (best site in tract)
metrics.measures: How many of DCA's location points the best spot in this tract earns, scored by SiteLine: nearby amenities, transit, school quality, neighborhood stability, special designations, distance from recent LIHTC awards, local housing need (Other Metro only), and historic districts.
metrics.targets: The location-based scoring criteria of the 2024–2025 QAP (§XI–§XXII), worth up to 46 points. Every point here counts directly toward DCA's score.
metrics.description: The highest total SiteLine score among the tract's grid cells: the best location score a site in this tract could earn.

metrics.label: Federal basis boost (QCT or DDA)
metrics.qap_ref: Core Plan §V, State-Designated Basis Boost, p. 15; §XIV.A, p. 104
metrics.source: HUD QCT and Small Area DDA, 2026
metrics.measures: Whether the tract is a 2026 Qualified Census Tract or sits in a 2026 Small Area Difficult Development Area, the two federal designations that unlock a 30% basis boost.
metrics.targets: Deal feasibility rather than points: the boost raises eligible basis, so the project gets more credits and pencils more easily (Core Plan §V). A QCT also adds 1 point under §XIV when the site is in a revitalization plan area.
metrics.description: Yes if the tract is a 2026 Qualified Census Tract or its center is in a 2026 Small Area DDA. Up to 30% more eligible basis means more credits per project. A QCT also adds 1 point under §XIV when the site is in a revitalization plan area.

metrics.label: Years since last award in the local government
metrics.qap_title: Competitive Rounds: tiebreakers and award limits
metrics.measures: How many years since the city (or the county, for unincorporated land) last received a LIHTC award. No award on record counts as best.
metrics.targets: DCA's 9% tiebreaker, which favors the local government with the oldest last award, and the cap of two Metro Pool awards per local government per round (Core Plan §V).
metrics.description: Years since the most recent LIHTC award in the tract's city (or the county, if unincorporated). In the 9% round, ties go to the local government whose last award is oldest, and each local government can win at most two Metro Pool awards per round. Blank = no award on record (best case).

metrics.label: Existing LIHTC units per 100 renter households
metrics.measures: Existing LIHTC low-income units per 100 renter households in the tract. Fewer is better.
metrics.targets: The market study threshold (Threshold §IV): capture rates must stay at or under 30% in Metro Pools, and the project can't hurt existing tax-credit properties.
metrics.description: How saturated the tract already is with LIHTC. The market study must show capture rates at or under 30% in Metro Pools and no adverse impact on existing tax-credit properties; failing it disqualifies the application.

metrics.label: Inland flood risk (FEMA)
metrics.measures: FEMA's inland flood risk score for the tract, which blends flood hazard with property exposure and community vulnerability. Off by default; lookups show the FEMA flood zone at the exact spot instead.
metrics.targets: DCA's environmental review (Threshold §VI), where floodplains and floodways add cost and risk. It's pass/fail, not points.
metrics.description: FEMA's inland flooding risk score (0-100) for the tract. Off by default: DCA treats floodplains as a pass/fail environmental issue, not as points, and this tract score also reflects property exposure and social vulnerability. The address lookup checks FEMA's flood map at the exact spot and shows a warning instead. The backtest can turn it back on if the evidence supports it.
